newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Last multinational force troops leave Albania.
newsitem.headline: Last multinational force troops leave Albania.

text.p: General Luciano Forlani, commander of the multinational protection force in Albania, led the last troops out of the troubled Balkan country on Monday and declared the mission a success.
"The mission was very positive....its target was achieved in a very efficient way," the Italian said at Rinas airport, 25 km (15 miles) north of the capital Tirana.

Italy spearheaded the force of some 7,000 soldiers from 10 nations deployed across Albania in April after a violent uprising, ignited by the collapse of get-rich-quick savings schemes, left the army and police in disarray and state authority in tatters.
Operation Alba (Italian for dawn) aimed to protect convoys of humanitarian aid and ensure free general elections could be held in relative calm.

The multinational force was criticised by some for not intervening to stop the violence of the past months, which has killed more than 1,500 Albanians. One foreign soldier died from a grenade explosion and up to eight others were slightly injured from stray bullets.
Albanian Defence Minister Sabit Brokaj presented Albania's Mother Teresa Award to General Forlani on Friday and praised his mission's efforts, especially in assisting in the general election.
Lieutenant Colonel Giovanni Bernardi told Reuters nine Italian officers would stay behind to continue talks with the Albanian defence ministry on restructuring the armed forces.
Former Albanian president Sali Berisha's Democratic Party government was forced to resign early this year after being blamed for allowing the shady pyramid investment funds to flourish.
An interim 10-party government led the country to the June 29 general election which was overwhelmingly won by a leftist coalition led by the Socialists.
